sections.name: resetDb
sections.title: Clearing the test database
sections.what: Empties all app tables so each test begins with no leftover data, keeping migration history and the five sports list.
sections.why: Likely reason: independent tests need a known starting state.
sections.watch_out: Clears every table in the connected database, so the connection must point only at the test schema.

sections.name: makeUser
sections.title: Creating a test user
sections.what: Creates a user with a unique name, email and fake password hash, and returns only the id, name and email.
sections.why: The comment says the fake hash lets tests prove a hash never leaks to outside code.
sections.watch_out: The returned object is intentionally small, so tests needing more fields must query again.

summary: Test helpers that empty the test database for a fresh start and create a test user with a fake password hash.
purpose: Gives every database test a clean starting point and a quick way to make users.
why: Likely reason: tests must not see data left by earlier tests. The fake hash lets tests check that real hashes never leak.
how: resetDb lists all tables in the current schema except migration history and the Sport list, empties them together, and restarts their counters. makeUser creates a user with a unique name, a unique email and a placeholder hash, and returns only id, name and email.
inputs: An optional name for makeUser. A database connection through the shared prisma client.
outputs: resetDb returns nothing. makeUser returns a small user object.
risks: resetDb deletes everything in whatever database the connection points to, so a connection to real data would destroy it. It builds a raw SQL command from table names, which is safe here only because the names come from the database itself.
debug: If tests see leftover data, check that resetDb ran and that the connection points to the test schema. If makeUser fails on email, check the counter.
